If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{({x}^{2}-1)^{2}-1}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[({x}^{2}-1)^{2}-1]}^{′}}{{[{x}^{2}]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4x({x}^{2}-1)}{2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4{x}^{3}-4x}{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{({x}^{2}-1)^{2}-1}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4{x}^{3}-4x}{2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[4{x}^{3}-4x]^{′}}{[2x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{12{x}^{2}-4}{2} \\  & =\frac{12(0)^{2}-4}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
